title: magic
summary: Generate magic squares in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Computed on the host CPU. Automatically resident inputs gather transparently; explicit gpuArray input is unsupported.

description: `magic(n)` returns a double `n`-by-`n` matrix. The order is `floor(real(double(n(1))))`, so array and complex inputs use their first real element. Construction rules across odd/even orders follow MATLAB semantics.
behaviors: `magic(n)` accepts documented numeric and character classes, selects the first real element, floors it, and requires the resulting order to be non-negative and representable.
`magic(1)` returns `1`, while `magic(0)` returns an empty `0 x 0` matrix.
`magic(2)` returns the documented degenerate matrix `[1 3;4 2]`, which is not a true magic square.
Odd, doubly-even (`n % 4 == 0`), and singly-even (`n % 4 == 2`) orders each use MATLAB's standard construction so results match MATLAB outputs.

examples.description: Use magic squares as structured input

faqs.question: Is `magic(2)` a true magic square?
faqs.answer: No. It returns `[1 3;4 2]` for compatibility, even though no true 2x2 magic square exists.

faqs.question: What happens when `n` is an array?
faqs.answer: The first element controls the order after taking its real part and flooring it. Use `ones`, `zeros`, or `eye` when you need a size-vector form.

faqs.question: How do I move the result to the GPU?
faqs.answer: Call `gpuArray(magic(n))` if you need the output on the GPU. RunMat computes `magic` on the host today.

gpu_residency: `magic` always runs on the host CPU today. If you need the result on the GPU, wrap the call in `gpuArray(...)`.
gpu_behavior: RunMat transparently gathers automatically resident inputs before evaluating `magic` and returns a host tensor. Explicit gpuArray input is rejected because the documented API does not support it.
